title: Source Prioritization Policy Counterexamples and Mathematical Proofs
description: Formal counterexamples establishing why naive probability summation, zero-unrated assumptions, and raw hop counting violate security decision-making.

counterexamples.name: Path Probability Summation Exceeds Unity and Distorts Risk
counterexamples.flawed_policy: Sum probabilities of alternative attack paths from the same source: P_total = sum(P_i)
counterexamples.scenario: Source Workstation-01 has two distinct attack paths to Domain Admins via Kerberoasting two different service accounts (SQL-Svc and Web-Svc).

flawed_calculation.mathematical_violation: Probability exceeds 1.0; violates Kolmogorov's axioms of probability theory.

counterexamples.statistical_flaw: Attack paths are not mutually exclusive events (A cap B != empty). Both paths share the common prerequisite of KDC reachability and local attacker offline cracking compute. Summing assumes complete mutual exclusivity, severely exaggerating the attacker success likelihood.
counterexamples.sound_policy: Retain individual path likelihoods as conditional intervals [p_lower, p_upper] on Pareto-optimal Min-Effort candidates. Never sum path probabilities across alternative routes.

counterexamples.name: Treating Unrated Likelihood as Zero Causes Fatal Blindspots
counterexamples.flawed_policy: Assign P=0 (or lowest rank) to paths with missing or unrated likelihood basis
counterexamples.scenario: Source Host-A has two alternative avenues to compromise the Domain Controller.

paths.mechanism: Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD) via machine account quota
Spearphishing DA over 3 hops with high effort

flawed_ranking.rationale: path-phishing-rated has P=[0.05, 0.10] > 0, while path-rbcd-unrated has P=0 (unrated treated as impossible).

counterexamples.security_consequence: Catastrophic false negative. Defenders deploy mitigations against the noisy, high-effort 12-step phishing route while completely ignoring the trivial 2-step RBCD attack path that allows full DC takeover.
counterexamples.sound_policy: Unrated paths retain likelihood_status='unrated' and participate fully in Min-Effort and Target Impact evaluations. A path with low effort (C=2) to a Catastrophic target is classified as Critical/High priority even when P is unrated.

counterexamples.name: Shortest Hop Count Misleading vs True Min-Effort
counterexamples.flawed_policy: Prioritize sources based on fewest graph hops (BloodHound shortest-path default)
counterexamples.scenario: Comparing two attack routes from Host-B to Domain Admins.

paths.description: Direct online password guessing against DA account; lockout risk and massive SOC detection.
Three automated structural hops with near-zero friction and zero credential cracking.

flawed_ranking.rationale: 1 hop is shorter than 3 hops in unweighted graph traversal.

counterexamples.security_consequence: Defenders focus on the 1-hop path which is practically unfeasible due to account lockouts, while the attacker trivially walks the 3-hop low-effort delegation chain.
counterexamples.sound_policy: Min-Effort uses additive task-based work-unit rubrics rather than structural edge counts. The 3-hop path with C=2.0 is correctly recognized as far easier than the 1-hop path with C=10.0.

counterexamples.name: Cross-Target Effort/Probability Equivalence Fallacy
counterexamples.flawed_policy: Rank sources solely on minimum effort without conditioning on target consequence
counterexamples.scenario: Source Workstation-01 reaches a Printer server in 1 step; Source Workstation-02 reaches the Primary DC in 2 steps.
counterexamples.security_consequence: Incident response triages a compromised printer workstation ahead of an imminent Active Directory domain takeover.
counterexamples.sound_policy: Hierarchical lexicographical ranking: Target Impact (Catastrophic > High > Medium > Low) strictly dominates Min-Effort. Workstation-02 is ranked Critical Rank 1, while Workstation-01 is ranked Low.
